purpose: Compare protest-day network-control behavior across five countries while separating political timing, network centralization, filtering mechanism, vendor lineage and foreign control-plane attribution.

Belarus.network_pattern: Repeated protest/election-conditioned national and mobile Internet restrictions in a centralized state-controlled international connectivity environment.
Belarus.lineage: Russian SORM lineage confirmed/strongly supported; protest-era DPI associated publicly with Sandvine supplied through Russian integrator Jet Infosystems.

Cuba.network_pattern: Repeated protest-conditioned national/regional restrictions on state monopoly ETECSA/AS27725; OONI/NetBlocks observed selective platform blocking and TCP RST/TLS-handshake interference.
Cuba.lineage: Recorded Future assesses Russian SORM procurement very likely, most notably Protei; ETECSA is listed as Protei customer; 2024 Protei-Movitel agreement. Chinese infrastructure is a major alternative lineage.

Kazakhstan.network_pattern: Repeated protest-conditioned local/national degradation and historical path-dependent HTTPS interception; 2026 filtering anomalies remain under ASN/path drill-down.
Kazakhstan.lineage: Russian SORM vendor lineage strongly supported; separate DPI evidence includes Allot, preventing simplistic Russian-equipment attribution.

Georgia.network_pattern: Severe and prolonged protest repression without a stable historic protest-to-shutdown pattern; small 2026 anomalies remain YELLOW.
Georgia.lineage: Domestic lawful-interception capability exists; Russian public-network SORM/TSPU vendor lineage not established.

Serbia.network_pattern: Large protests without established national Internet shutdown pattern; 15 March 2025 GNSS jamming/spoofing treated as a separate RF mechanism, not DPI/TSPU.
Serbia.lineage: No established Russian TSPU/SORM public-network control lineage relevant to protest-day Internet behavior.

cross_country_findings: PROTEST alone has zero attribution weight: Georgia and Serbia provide strong negative controls.
CENTRALIZED NETWORK CONTROL materially increases the feasibility of repeatable protest-conditioned restrictions: Belarus and Cuba are the clearest positive controls.
Russian-origin SORM vendor presence is not sufficient to infer that Russian equipment performs censorship, that a TSPU-like mechanism is deployed, or that Moscow controls the system remotely.

Cuba materially strengthens the global Spider because it combines a centralized state monopoly ASN, independently measured RST/DPI behavior, repeated protest-day restrictions, and a documented Russian SORM vendor relationship in the same national environment.

The critical missing bridge across all foreign cases is DEVICE/CONTROL-CHANNEL CAUSALITY: public evidence rarely links a measured block/reset to a specific vendor appliance, firmware/control server or foreign operator command path.

Power-grid failures are a mandatory confound in Cuba and some Kazakhstan windows; physical repression and spyware are separate mechanisms in Georgia/Serbia and must not be counted as network filtering evidence.
Matching timing across countries contributes no remote-control attribution without matching packet fingerprint, path localization and control/vendor bridge.

cisa_gate_implications.reason: Cuba now satisfies most historical technical dimensions, but public evidence still does not causally bind the measured DPI/reset/shutdown mechanism to a Russian SORM device/control channel, and the 2026 protest-day outage signal is not yet independently mechanism-localized.
red_trigger_needed: current reproducible foreign-vantage path-specific filtering affecting US/open services
specific device/vendor/control-channel bridge or cross-country matching fingerprint

epistemic_firewall: same political event != same network mechanism
same product family != same control plane
Russian-origin vendor presence != Russian remote command
temporal coincidence alone = zero attribution weight
